indicator_definition: The severe housing deprivation rate is the proportion of the population living in an overcrowded dwelling that also lacks at least one of the following: a bath or shower, an indoor flushing toilet, or has a leaking roof or damp walls. It is expressed as a percentage. Data are based on EU-SILC.
rationale: Adequate housing is a fundamental human need and a key determinant of health and well-being. Severe housing deprivation directly impacts physical and mental health, educational attainment and social participation. Progress means a sustained reduction in the severe housing deprivation rate.
methodology_characteristics: Data are collected through EU-SILC. Overcrowding is assessed relative to household size and composition. Housing quality deprivation covers structural problems (leaking roof, damp walls) and the absence of basic facilities (bath or shower, indoor toilet).
